comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Issue #⁠245596 reports the Shoper cookie-consent dialog on www⁠.4motos.pl ("Dbamy o Twoją prywatność") plus its dark page mask; the reporter profile reproduced both. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the overlay and its mask was validated in the extension (symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no remaining instances), so I propose it for the Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `4motos.pl##.consents__wrapper, .consents__mask` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance (a first-party Shoper consent dialog plus its page mask), which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter is meant to handle; the run instruction closes no rule category for it:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall. No anti-adblock, malware or paywall policy rule applies; the page shows a plain consent overlay. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9941b7d3307202ca616dd93a3e5bddd9e5997ffd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40604415016 Automated analysis against filters at `9941b7d`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

issue.title: www.eneba.com
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder

### What product do you use?
Other ad blocker: AdBlocker Ultimate on Firefox, whose Ultimate Privacy Filter carries the same rule. The rule comes from the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, so AdGuard users are affected the same way.

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website doesn't work properly: Eneba's partner referral cookie is removed, so purchases are not credited to the partner who sent the buyer.

### Description
The generic rule `$cookie=af_id` in the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter removes the first-party cookie `af_id` on www.eneba.com.

Eneba's affiliate links carry `?af_id=<partner>`. When the page loads, Eneba's own script sets `af_id=<partner>` on www.eneba.com for 30 days, and that cookie is what credits the partner when the buyer checks out. If the cookie is removed, the referral is lost. Nothing cross-site is involved: it is Eneba's own cookie on its own domain.

The rule sits right next to `$cookie=afUserId`, so it looks aimed at AppsFlyer's cookies. On eneba.com the same name is used for something else.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Without the filter, open https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder
2. The page sets the cookie `af_id=keyfinder` on www.eneba.com, expiring in 30 days.
3. With the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter on, `$cookie=af_id` removes that cookie, so Eneba has nothing to credit at checkout.

A real case: on 26 Oct 2026 a buyer on Firefox with AdBlocker Ultimate clicked our link at 18:17 UTC and ordered at 18:18 UTC. Eneba did not credit the referral. Our other Eneba referrals from browsers without this rule are credited normally.

### Suggested fix
```
@@||eneba.com^$cookie=af_id
```

### Disclosure
We run keyfinder.gg, a game key price comparison site, and we are an Eneba affiliate, so this affects us directly. It also affects every creator and site in Eneba's partner program whose audience uses AdGuard or AdBlocker Ultimate.

issue.title: www.eneba.com
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder

### What product do you use?
Other ad blocker: AdBlocker Ultimate on Firefox, whose Ultimate Privacy Filter carries the same rule. The rule comes from the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter, so AdGuard users are affected the same way.

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website doesn't work properly: Eneba's partner referral cookie is removed, so purchases are not credited to the partner who sent the buyer.

### Description
The generic rule `$cookie=af_id` in the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter removes the first-party cookie `af_id` on www.eneba.com.

Eneba's affiliate links carry `?af_id=<partner>`. When the page loads, Eneba's own script sets `af_id=<partner>` on www.eneba.com for 30 days, and that cookie is what credits the partner when the buyer checks out. If the cookie is removed, the referral is lost. Nothing cross-site is involved: it is Eneba's own cookie on its own domain.

The rule sits right next to `$cookie=afUserId`, so it looks aimed at AppsFlyer's cookies. On eneba.com the same name is used for something else.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Without the filter, open https://www.eneba.com/steam-mechabellum-pc-steam-key-global?af_id=keyfinder
2. The page sets the cookie `af_id=keyfinder` on www.eneba.com, expiring in 30 days.
3. With the AdGuard Tracking Protection filter on, `$cookie=af_id` removes that cookie, so Eneba has nothing to credit at checkout.

A real case: on 26 Oct 2026 a buyer on Firefox with AdBlocker Ultimate clicked our link at 18:17 UTC and ordered at 18:18 UTC. Eneba did not credit the referral. Our other Eneba referrals from browsers without this rule are credited normally.

### Suggested fix
```
@@||eneba.com^$cookie=af_id
```

### Disclosure
We run keyfinder.gg, a game key price comparison site, and we are an Eneba affiliate, so this affects us directly. It also affects every creator and site in Eneba's partner program whose audience uses AdGuard or AdBlocker Ultimate.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"4a1748b9a14ea9dd891e1011ee428dcf8e511e7fccf2e9d164915d4752b9c771"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On the reported Eneba URL the alleged breakage does not reproduce:⁠ with AdGuard Tracking Protection active the page renders intact, the affiliate referral is still captured (the 302 rewrites ?af_id= into utm_medium/utm_source and the site stores it in localStorage), eneba.com's other first-party cookies survive, and no af_id cookie was ever observed — even in the experiment phase where no rule applied. No rule change is supported, so the reporter's requested `@@||eneba.com^$cookie=af_id` exception is not proposed.

## Missing information

- No unfiltered control session in adguard_cli mode; reporter's third-party filter unavailable: In the locked adguard_cli environment every browser session routes through the filtering proxy:⁠ a session launched with extension:⁠"none" already applied AdGuard Tracking Protection filter rules (engine "AdGuard CLI", list id 3), and launch_browser refuses a "settings" object for extension:⁠"none", so no unfiltered baseline can be captured. For a report whose only symptom is a cookie being removed, that means the cookie's presence without filtering cannot be observed. Additionally, the engine's get_applied_rules states that it never logs the text of rules that modify a request ($cookie among them), and search_rules indexes only the URL portion of network rules, so the accused generic `$cookie=af_id` line could not be located in the repository or confirmed in the applied list. filterBaseline also reports skippedSources:⁠ {"kind":⁠"unresolved_name","reportedName":⁠"Ultimate Privacy Filter"} — the reporter's third-party list is not inspectable here.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40615468340

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported Yandex 403 page on n1960529.yclients.ru did not reproduce:⁠ with the AdGuard CLI filtering proxy (HTTPS interception active) the site loaded twice with HTTP 200, redirected to its booking menu and rendered fully, and no repository rule targets yclients.ru. No filter rule change is needed for this report; the 403 most plausibly comes from outside the filter lists, which I could not test.

## Missing information

- Reporter's non-official sources (EasyList Cookie, 3 blocklists, 7 AnnoyancesFilter custom subscriptions) cannot be loaded in this environment: The adguard_cli baseline advertises only official AdGuard filters (1,2,3,11,17,18,20,21,25) and lists 12 reporter sources under skippedSources (EasyList Cookie List, Online Malicious URL Blocklist, Phishing URL Blocklist, Scam Blocklist by DurableNapkin, uBlock Origin - Badware risks, and the seven AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/*.txt custom subscriptions). No tool offered a way to load those sources, so the reporter's exact filter set - in particular the antiadblock/popups subscriptions and EasyList Cookie - could not be reproduced. Also, the reporter's HTTPS-filtering path runs inside AdGuard for Android's own network stack on Firefox Preview, which no available environment reproduces exactly; no geographic proxy backend is available, so an egress-IP-dependent server response cannot be tested.

comment.body:
I had initially tested on MacOS Safari and Chrome, FireFox for checking leftover is disappear. 

It also works on iOS Safari. I've tested with following rules after received your question. 

```adblock
! disable the delete rules
mail.yahoo.com#@%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'AppBootstrapData.config.adshieldAdblockRecovery', 'false', '', '', 'true')
mail.yahoo.com#@%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'AppState.reduxState.features.adshieldAdblockRecovery', 'false', '', '', 'true')
@@||mail.yahoo.com$replace=/("adshield(Adblock|NativeAd)Recovery"):true/\$1:false/
mail.yahoo.com#@%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'AppState.reduxState.features.adshieldAdblockRecovery', 'false')
mail.yahoo.com#@%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'AppState.reduxState.features.ads', 'false')
mail.yahoo.com#@%#//scriptlet('set-constant', 'AppState.reduxState.features.pencilAd', 'false')
! merged rules
mail.yahoo.com#%#//scriptlet('trusted-replace-node-text', 'script', '/App(State|BootstrapData) = /', '/"(ads|pencilAd|secondPencilAd|thirdPencilAd|infinitePencilAd|searchAd|secondSearchAd|additionalPencilAdWithSearchAd|sameSearchAdOnSecondPencil|adshieldAdblockRecovery|adshieldNativeAdRecovery)":true/g', '"$1":false')
```

Reproduced the in-player pre-roll on www⁠.yifan.tv with the reporter's own AdGuard profile, but it is served entirely by the site's own ad platform (ad orders from ppt.yifan.tv/play/o, creatives from pptstatic.yifan.tv, played inside the site's own player stream) with no third-party ad network involved, and blocking that order endpoint did not remove it. Under the run instruction's policy ("The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing") no rule should be written, so this report is recommended for closing.

## Still visible after the rule

- VG-PLAYER#⁠main-player / 广告 / HONOR Magic9 — The main video player shows an in-player pre-roll advertisement:⁠ a HONOR Magic9 brand creative occupies the right portion of the player, with the 广告 label visible at the lower right of the player area.
- Main video player (VG-PLAYER#⁠main-player), right half of the player area — In-player pre-roll ad creative:⁠ HONOR Magic9 series brand advertisement (product images of phones and camera lens, '荣耀Magic9 系列' and HONOR logo) filling the right portion of the video player, with a small '广告' label at the bottom-right corner of the player frame.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The KB filter policy states the same rule:⁠ "The site’s own advertising should not be deliberately blocked. However, it should not be unblocked if the blocking is caused by general filtering rules" (AdguardTeam/KnowledgeBase docs/general/ad-filtering/filter-policy.md). Every advertising request on the reported play page is first-party to the site:⁠ the ad order comes from https:⁠//ppt.yifan.tv/play/o, the banner creatives from pptstatic.yifan.tv/upload/video/*.jpg, the ad configuration from the site's own localStorage key ggs_20xx, and the in-player pre-roll is played inside the site's own player (VG-PLAYER#⁠main-player) from the site's own HLS stream on sss111-e1.pipecdn.vip. No third-party advertising network request exists in either captured session; the only third-party ad host, pagead2.googlesyndication.com, is already redirected by the AdGuard Base filter and is used by the site only for its own ad-block probe (window.detectAdBlock()). The advertising is therefore the site's own (first-party) advertising, which this repository's policy excludes from deliberate blocking; recommend closing the report instead of writing a rule.

## Missing information

- Filter policy does not define "the site's own advertising (first-party ads)": The run instruction's policy bullet "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing" and the KB filter-policy bullet "The site's own advertising should not be deliberately blocked" are the only statements available, and neither defines the term. lookup_rule_guidance(topic=policy) returns only that summary bullet; the "Ad blocking filters → Terminology" section of the same document (which would define first-party/site advertising) is never served, even when queried with "Terminology first-party advertising". This run needed that definition to decide whether a pre-roll brand advertisement (HONOR Magic9) delivered entirely by the site's own ad platform (ppt.yifan.tv ad orders, pptstatic.yifan.tv creatives) counts as the site's own advertising or as third-party advertising served first-party.

## Artifacts

issue.body:
# 죄송합니다. Umanle S.R.L.가 AdGuard의 광고 차단을 방해하고 있습니다.

나무위키 운영사인 Umanle S.R.L.가 나무위키의 DOM 구조를 관련된 필터 업데이트가 있을 때 마다 변경하므로 필터로 차단하기에는 오차단이 발생할 수 있습니다.

또한, Umanle S.R.L.가 기술적인 안티-애드블록하여 의도적으로 나무위키 문서를 읽을 수 없게 했던 점과 전용 유저스크립트인 NamuLink의 차단 방법을 우회하게끔 네이버 파워링크 광고 알고리즘을 업데이트합니다.

## 유저스크립트 설치

[NamuLink 유저스크립트](https://github.com/List-KR/NamuLink)를 설치하여 나무위키의 파워링크 광고를 차단하실 수 있습니다.
한국어로 작성되어 있는 설치 방법은 [이 URL](https://community.list-kr.com/docs/AdGuard/Userscripts/NamuLink)를 클릭하여 확인해주세요.


## 그래도 문제가 있으신가요?
유저스크립트를 사용했을 때 발생하는 문제는 [이 이슈 트래커](https://github.com/List-KR/NamuLink/issues)로 알려주세요.
기타 문제는 [이 곳](https://github.com/List-KR/List-KR/issues)으로 알려주세요.
GitHub 이슈를 사용하시기 어렵다면, filters@adguard.com 로 문의해주세요.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"0cdab394eeae514c4a2f014a511fa3248c71654a0d2118d9c779b891c2f87ec5"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported automatic download on www⁠.opera.com/de/computer/thanks is opera.com's own first-party download flow:⁠ a hidden 1x1px iframe id="download-this" in the served HTML pointing at net.geo.opera.com/opera/stable/windows, plus the page's own "Download didn't start? Click here." fallback link. No anti-adblock wall or detector script was observed and the download fires identically with and without the ad blocker, so the repository policy gives first-party self-promotion no rule — recommend closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Repository policy (run instruction):⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The reported automatic download is opera.com's own first-party download of its own product:⁠ a hidden 1x1px iframe id="download-this" in the served HTML pointing at net.geo.opera.com/opera/stable/windows (thirdParty:⁠false), with the page's own fallback link "Download didn't start? Click here." next to it. The anti-adblock premise of the label is not supported by what the page shows:⁠ no anti-adblock wall, message or content gate is present, no detector script appears in the captured requests, and the download fires identically in the unfiltered control session and in the reporter-profile session with the reporter's filters enabled. The agent never closes an issue:⁠ this is a recommendation to close, for a maintainer to check and decide.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40642425689

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — chemi-plast.pl serves a first-party, fixed bottom cookie-consent panel ("COOKIES I ZGODY") that no baseline list hides. The domain-scoped rule `chemi-plast.pl##.consent-banner` was verified to remove it with the page left intact, and it extends the existing shared `.consent-banner` rule in the Cookies filter. ## Rule `chemi-plast.pl##.consent-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a cookie-consent notice (annoyance), not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The consent UI is first-party (served from /assets/index-*.js), so a cosmetic element-hiding rule is the appropriate fix; there is no detector script or third-party vendor to block. An existing shared rule already covers the exact selector `.consent-banner`, and the maintainer rules direct extending that shared rule rather than writing a new per-site expression. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d194f556be76aea75abc0aedd953e74216b30602/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 13831](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d194f556be76aea75abc0aedd953e74216b30602/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L13831). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — pasgoliptv44.site carries two `div.reklam-3` ad banner units (image `pasgoltvgif.webp`, alt="reklamlar") and a header announcement line, all wrapped in `` — the same advertising short link the reporter says every annotated element redirects to. The domain-scoped hide `pasgoliptv44.site##.header-text, .reklam-3` was verified:⁠ all three matched elements hidden, symptom resolved, page integrity intact. ## Rule `pasgoliptv44.site##.header-text, .reklam-3` ## Policy rationale The report is an ad-serving issue, not a paywall, German anti-adblock wall, or scam/phishing page, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The hidden elements are advertising units (class "reklam", img alt="reklamlar") and a promotional header line carrying the site's affiliate short link, not the site's own content; the repo already blocks the same `.reklam-3` class on the sibling site betanotv6.site. No existing rule in this repository covers pasgoliptv44.site (domain inventory:⁠ 0 matches), so a new domain-scoped rule is required. ## Place in the list [TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/77d1c8eb1d59cb872b0039a2296e70ac51c2755c/TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40644426077 Automated analysis against filters at `77d1c8e`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — libermedia.pl shows a YOOtheme cookie-consent panel (`.tm-consent`, fixed bottom right, ACCEPT / REJECT / MANAGE SETTINGS) covering the right-hand article card; the repository already has a shared rule for this exact panel, so the fix is the domain-scoped rule `libermedia.pl##.tm-consent`, which apply_rule verified (visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact, no remaining instances). ## Rule `libermedia.pl##.tm-consent` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance:⁠ a first-party cookie-consent notice, which is exactly what the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for; it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's close-or-hand-off rules applies. Maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them' applies:⁠ the fix fits an existing shared rule for this consent panel, so the reported domain is added to that rule instead of a new expression being written. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d194f556be76aea75abc0aedd953e74216b30602/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 878](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d194f556be76aea75abc0aedd953e74216b30602/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L878). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40640569996 Automated analysis against filters at `d194f55`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.
